doc.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Great uncle's records and the Massey Hall concert
summary: His great uncle gave him jazz albums; the Massey Hall concert changed his life, along with Ron Carter and Paul Chambers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well with your father playing rhythm & blues, and you being a James Brown fan, how was it that you got an interest in “Stars Fell on Alabama” for instance?

My great uncle, the bass player. He was the man in the family that had all of the albums. So when he discovered I was taking acoustic bass lessons in junior high school he was so happy, he brought me over a big stack of albums to listen to. He said, “Well now that you’re playing the acoustic bass, I want you to listen to these records.” So the one record

that was in there that changed my life forever was the Massey Hall Concert with Bird and Dizzy, Bud Powell, Charles Mingus and Max Roach. And the group sound of that record. You know because I mean I was, we’re talking like 1984, so I was into Prince and Michael Jackson, everything that was hot at that time. And I still listen to that as well as checking out Bird and Miles and it was a different kind of energy. But the joy and the feeling was still there. So fortunately I was able to latch on to it you know. And then I heard bass players like Ron Carter and Paul Chambers and I said man, so that’s how this instrument is supposed to be played.
